text: In the dual-rail encoding used by linear optical quantum computing, a logical qubit is:
choices: Two photons in a single mode
The intensity level of a classical laser beam
One photon shared between two modes: |0>_L = |1,0> and |1>_L = |0,1>
The spin of an electron trapped in a quantum dot
explanation: Dual-rail encodes one photon across two modes, so |0>_L = |1,0> and |1>_L = |0,1>; a U(2) mode transformation then acts directly as the single-qubit gate. It uses one photon, not two (choice 0); it is not a classical intensity (choice 1); and photonic qubits here are photon occupancy, not electron spin (choice 3).
